NOTE:  PUBLIC PARTICIPATION INFORMATION
  Pursuant to the Governor's Executive Order N-29-20 and current State and County Public Health Orders,
  City Council Members will be participating via teleconference.

  - City Council meetings are recorded and live-streamed on the City’s website at www.rhe.city and
  available for viewing thereafter, and televised on Cox 33 and Frontier FiOS 38 on Wednesday and Friday
  following the meeting.

  - Members of the public may listen to the meeting live by calling: (1-669-900-6833) from any phone,
  Meeting ID: 827 7299 9410, Meeting Password: 066081. (Please note you will not have the ability to
  speak using the call-in option from a phone line.)

  - Public correspondence may be emailed to the City Clerk at cityclerk@rollinghillsestatesca.gov. Emails
  received before 3:00 p.m. the night of the Council meeting will be forwarded to the City Council for their
  consideration and included as part of the record.

  - Members of the public may comment online using eComment on the “Meeting Agendas, Minutes &
  Videos” page of the City’s website (www.rhe.city/MeetingAgendas). Once the agenda is published, there
  will be an “eComment” button next to the linked agenda under "Upcoming Events". Follow this link to
  the City’s SpeakUp page. After you register, you may comment on any item on that particular agenda.
  These comments can be seen by the public, will be considered by the Council and become part of the
  record.

  - Members of the public who wish to speak during this meeting may join the Zoom meeting by accessing the
  Zoom app from a computer (downloaded at Zoom.com) or tablet or phone (downloaded in the App Store),
  by entering the following credentials: Meeting ID: 827 7299 9410, Meeting Password: 066081. Members
  of the public who join the Zoom meeting will not have video, and may request to speak using the following
  process: After joining the Zoom meeting, if you wish to speak, please select the "raise hand" option at the
  lower portion of your screen. The City Clerk will send you a chat message to identify which item on the
  agenda you would like to speak on and will unmute your mic at the appropriate time.

  Agenda reports and other disclosable public records relating to each Open Session agenda item are
  available on the City's website under Meeting Agendas, Minutes & Videos at www.rhe.city.

MINUTES
  CITY COUNCIL MEETING
  MARCH 23, 2021

1.  CALL MEETING TO ORDER

A regular meeting of the City Council of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was called to order
by MAYOR ZUCKERMAN at 7:58 p.m. via teleconference, pursuant to the Governor’s
Executive Order N-29-20 and current State and County Public Health Orders.

2.  SALUTE TO THE FLAG

Flag salute led by MAYOR ZUCKERMAN.

3.  ROLL CALL

City Council Members Present:  Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan and Zuckerman

City Council Members Absent:  None

City Staff Present:  City Manager Greg Grammer
  City Attorney Don Davis
  Assistant City Manager Alexa Davis
  Planning Manager Jeannie Naughton
  Community Development & PW Director David Wahba
  Community Services Supervisor Cynthia Morquecho
  Interim City Clerk Carrie Gallagher

4.  CEREMONIAL ITEMS

A.  WASTE MANAGEMENT "RECYCLING HERO" DRAWING FOR ONE YEAR OF FREE
  RESIDENTIAL AND COMMERCIAL REFUSE SERVICE FIRST QUARTER 2021

  Sharon Shapiro-Fox of Waste Management drew names for the 1st quarter winners
  to receive one free year of service: FIRST QUARTER RESIDENTIAL WINNER: 48
  Shady Vista Rd. FIRST QUARTER COMMERCIAL WINNER: Silver Spur LLC.

5.  CONSENT CALENDAR

The following routine matters will be acted upon by one vote to approve with the majority
consent of the City Council. There will be no separate discussion of these items unless good
cause is shown by a member prior to the roll call vote. (Items removed for individual
consideration will be voted on separately.)

separate consideration.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  2
MARCH 23, 2021
 8.  NEW BUSINESS

A.  PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION ACTION ITEM OF MARCH 15, 2021
  PICKLEBALL PROPOSAL

Community Services Coordinator A-Haja provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA inquired on the timeline for determining if the temporary
conversion will become permanent. Community Services Coordinator A-Haja noted the City
intends to develop a community survey to better gage interest from the tennis community.

Assistant City Manager Davis added that staff anticipates rolling out the survey between
April and June. She stated that staff will return to Council with quantifiable date once input
is received and the survey is complete.

COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ asked if this conversion plan was the result of a decrease in
usage by the tennis community and Assistant City Manager Davis replied having received a
report from the tennis pro that afternoon usage of the courts is currently underutilized.

COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA inquired as to the source of funding for this project.
Assistant City Manager Davis replied that staff was looking at using park facilities fees.

City Manager Grammer added that the decision to make this project permanent could wait
until later in the year to provide staff time to better gage the communities’ interest.

MAYOR ZUCKERMAN agreed and added that he would like to hear input from the tennis
community.

Public comment was invited via email, via eComment on the City’s website, and during the live
Zoom Webinar as noticed on the Agenda and on the City’s website and social media platforms.

No public testimony was received.

  COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF moved, seconded by, COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA
  TO APPROVE THE TEMPORARY CONVERSION OF ONE TENNIS COURT TO
  PICKLEBALL COURTS AT ERNIE HOWLETT TENNIS CLUB WITH COURT
  UTILIZATION TIMES TO BE COORDINATED WITH THE TENNIS PRO AND
  RECOMMEND CONSIDERATION FOR PERMANENT COURT CONVERSION IN
  FUTURE COURT RESURFACING PROJECT.

  AYES:  Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan and Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  None

9.  OLD BUSINESS

MAYOR ZUCKERMAN reordered the agenda to hear item 9B prior to item 9A.

B.  PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION ACTION ITEM OF MARCH 15, 2021:
  NATURE CENTER CONCEPTUAL DESIGN

Assistant City Manager Davis provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF spoke regarding meeting the expectations of impacted
communities and inquired on input opportunities as it relates to parking, noise and use.
Assistant City Manager Davis noted that information will continue to be shared with the
community as the project progresses. She noted the use of an interested individuals email list
and shared that the City held early community meetings which led to this concept design. She
stated that the City is providing plenty of opportunity to keep the community engaged.

COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA inquired on budgeting for architects and environmental
consultants. City Manager Grammer replied that staff will return to Council for review and
approval of scope of work and proposals from both consultants.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  3
MARCH 23, 2021
 MAYOR ZUCKERMAN inquired on the possibility of enlarging trailhead parking and
questioned the need to satisfy existing municipal parking requirements prior to returning to
either the Planning Commission or City Council with a plan. Planning Manager Naughton
concurred noting that existing requirements will need to be addressed and analyzed in the
California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) document prior to review by Planning or Council.

Community Development & Public Works Director Wahba added that although not
previously studied in great detail, the option to enlarge trailhead parking could be discussed
in the EIR.

Discussion ensued over bike lanes in the area and mitigation options to avoid traffic cut
troughs.

Public comment was invited via email, via eComment on the City’s website, and during the live
Zoom Webinar as noticed on the Agenda and on the City’s website and social media platforms.

Dan Dreiling, Rolling Hills Estates resident, noted support for the project but voiced concern
over equestrian access.

Paul Moilanen, Rolling Hills Estates resident, voiced concern over expanded usage,
additional operating hours, safety, parking and traffic cut through concerns.

Assistant City Manager Davis noted having received three items of public comment all of which
were provided to City Council prior to the start of tonight’s meeting.

MAYOR ZUCKERMAN inquired regarding possible conditions of approval. City Staff noted that
viable options will be explored.

Mayor Pro Tem Zerunyan stated this is a beautiful project that will make the community proud,
he added that staff and Council are committed to a thoughtful process noting many efforts to
divert parking from Hitching Post.

  COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA moved, seconded by, MAYOR PRO TEM
  ZERUNYAN TO APPROVE THE GEORGE F CANYON NATURE CENTER
  CONCEPTUAL DESIGN AND DIRECTED STAFF TO RETURN WITH AGREEMENTS
  FOR THE ARCHITECT TO CONTINUE WORK TOWARD FINAL PLAN AND
  SPECIFICATIONS AND AN ENVIRONMENTAL CONSULTANT FOR AN
  ENVIRONMENTAL REVIEW.

  AYES:  Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan and Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  None

A.  RESOLUTION NO. 2474 PROPOSITION 68 TRANSFER FUNDS UPDATE

Community Services Supervisor Morquecho provided a staff report (as per the agenda
material).

COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA inquired regarding which project these funds would go
towards; staff confirmed that funds would be earmarked for the Nature Center Project.

Public comment was invited via email, via eComment on the City’s website, and during the live
Zoom Webinar as noticed on the Agenda and on the City’s website and social media platforms.

No public testimony was received.

COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF, TO
ADOPT RESOLUTION NO. 2474 AND ACCEPT ADDITIONAL PROPOSITION 68 URBAN
PER CAPITA FUNDS TRANSFERRED IN THE AMOUNT OF $1, 156 FROM THE CITY OF
ROLLING HILLS.

  AYES:  Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan and Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  None

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  4
MARCH 23, 2021
 C.  UPDATE ON LOS ANGELES COUNTY SAFER AT HOME ORDER AND STATUS OF
  CITY EVENTS (VERBAL REPORT)

City Manager Grammer noted a decline in COVID-19 hospitalizations and deaths in the County
as well as an increase in the number of vaccines being administered, he added that the County
recently moved from the purple tier to the red tier allowing for more openings and loosening of
restrictions. He added that the County is meeting the matrix for the orange tier and if it continues
we could be looking at moving into the orange tier very soon to further loosen restrictions
allowing for greater capacity at stores and restaurants. He introduced Cynthia Morquecho who
provided an update on City events. She stated that the City would host a Community Meeting
on Thursday March 25th to discuss playground equipment at Chandler Park, she noted a park
scavenger hunt to be held in early April to be hosted at different parks around the City, April
17 the City will host a Drive-in Movie Night Event at Ernie Howlett Park celebrating Earth Day
with the Movie WALL–E teaming up with Waste Management to provide handouts to children
in attendance, she included that staff is working towards scheduling the upcoming Mayor’s ride
and considering potential modifications due to COVID 19 restrictions.

  RECEIVED AND FILED SO ORDERED BY MAYOR ZUCKERMAN

10.  CITY ATTORNEY ITEMS

NONE.

11.  CITY COUNCIL/REGIONAL COMMITTEE REPORTS

A.  DRAFT SUPPORT LETTER SENATE BILL 612

Planning Manager Jeannie Naughton provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA noted her support for the bill and suggested including local
legislators to the recipient list; Planning Manager Naughton agreed to do so.

Public comment was invited via email, via eComment on the City’s website, and during the live
Zoom Webinar as noticed on the Agenda and on the City’s website and social media platforms.

No public testimony was received.

  COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA,
  TO AUTHORIZE THE MAYOR TO SIGN THE ATTACHED LETTER IN SUPPORT OF
  SENATE BILL 612.

  AYES:  Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan and Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  None

City Council Reports

COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF reported that the Equestrian Committee met and reviewed the
results of the Peter Weber Equestrian Center survey; she requested it be put on a future
agenda for Council to review.

COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF also reported on attending the Palos Verdes Peninsula Chamber
of Commerce Economic Forecast Breakfast, noting it having been well attended.

COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF also announced having attended a 2-day Regional Leadership
Forum with South Bay Cities Council of Government.

12.  MAYOR AND COUNCIL ITEMS

NONE.

13.  CLOSED SESSION

NONE.

MARCH 23, 2021
 14.  ADJOURNMENT

Rolling Hills Council Member Dr. Godfrey Pernell to the next meeting: Tuesday, April 13,
2021 at 7:00 p.m. via teleconference.
